title: GPT-3 and the 2020 Discovery of Few-Shot In-Context Learning
explainer: The core premise of prompt engineering - that a frozen model can perform a new task from a few examples placed in the prompt, with no retraining at all - was demonstrated at scale in the 2020 paper 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners,' which introduced GPT-3 and showed this in-context learning ability sharpening as model size grew. Before this result, the standard way to adapt a language model to a new task was to retrain its weights (fine-tuning), which is why prompting was initially treated as a curiosity rather than the primary interface it has become.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting and the 2022 Paper That Named It
explainer: Asking a model to reason step by step before answering, a staple technique in advanced prompting, was formally studied and named in a 2022 paper, 'Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models,' which found the technique helped mainly on large models and barely at all on small ones. That emergence-with-scale pattern is a useful caution: a prompting trick validated on one model size can quietly fail when you swap to a smaller or older model.
